hindi: मनुष्यों की जीविका अर्थ है; मनुष्यों से युक्त भूमि — यह अर्थ है।
english: The livelihood of men is artha (wealth); [it is] the earth inhabited by men — such is the meaning.
notes: 'ity arthaḥ' = iti arthaḥ 'such is the meaning'. The first arthaḥ (wealth, artha) and the last (meaning) are different senses.
lines_deva: मनुष्याणां वृत्तिर् अर्थः, मनुष्यवती भूमिर् इत्य् अर्थः
lines_iast: manuṣyāṇāṃ vṛttir arthaḥ, manuṣyavatī bhūmir ity arthaḥ

hindi: उस पृथ्वी की प्राप्ति और पालन के उपाय का शास्त्र अर्थशास्त्र कहलाता है।
english: The treatise [that is] the means of acquiring and protecting that earth [is called] the Arthaśāstra.
notes: 'iti' marks the name. 'pṛthivyā' is read as pṛthivyāḥ (gen.), sandhi before 'lābha'.
lines_deva: तस्याः पृथिव्या लाभ.पालन.उपायः शास्त्रम् अर्थ.शास्त्रम् इति
lines_iast: tasyāḥ pṛthivyā lābha.pālana.upāyaḥ śāstram artha.śāstram iti

hindi: वह बत्तीस युक्तियों से युक्त है — अधिकरण, विधान, योग, पदार्थ, हेत्वर्थ, उद्देश, निर्देश, उपदेश, अपदेश, अतिदेश, प्रदेश, उपमान, अर्थापत्ति, संशय, प्रसङ्ग, विपर्यय, वाक्यशेष, अनुमत, व्याख्यान, निर्वचन, निदर्शन, अपवर्ग, स्वसंज्ञा, पूर्वपक्ष, उत्तरपक्ष, एकान्त, अनागतावेक्षण, अतिक्रान्तावेक्षण, नियोग, विकल्प, समुच्चय, ऊह्य।
english: It is endowed with thirty-two devices (yukti) — adhikaraṇa, vidhāna, yoga, padārtha, hetvartha, uddeśa, nirdeśa, upadeśa, apadeśa, atideśa, pradeśa, upamāna, arthāpatti, saṃśaya, prasaṅga, viparyaya, vākyaśeṣa, anumata, vyākhyāna, nirvacana, nidarśana, apavarga, svasaṃjñā, pūrvapakṣa, uttarapakṣa, ekānta, anāgatāvekṣaṇa, atikrāntāvekṣaṇa, niyoga, vikalpa, samuccaya, ūhya.
notes: The thirty-two names are technical terms; the glosses in the word split are literal and are explained, largely in the order listed, in the following units (4-37). 'tad.dvātriṃśad' is joined by the editors with '.', but tat and dvātriṃśat are read as two words (it / thirty-two). Closing 'iti' ends the list and is not translated. The list has 32 names.
lines_deva: तद्.द्वात्रिंशद् युक्ति.युक्तं - अधिकरणम्, विधानम्, योगः, पद.अर्थः, हेत्व्.अर्थः, उद्देशः, निर्देशः, उपदेशः, अपदेशः, अतिदेशः, प्रदेशः, उपमानम्, अर्थ.आपत्तिः, संशयः, प्रसङ्गः, विपर्ययः, वाक्य.शेषः, अनुमतम्, व्याख्यानम्, निर्वचनम्, निदर्शनम्, अपवर्गः, स्व.सञ्ज्ञा, पूर्व.पक्षः, उत्तर.पक्षः, एक.अन्तः, अनागत.अवेक्षणम्, अतिक्रान्त.अवेक्षणम्, नियोगः, विकल्पः, समुच्चयः ऊह्यम् इति
lines_iast: tad.dvātriṃśad yukti.yuktaṃ - adhikaraṇam, vidhānam, yogaḥ, pada.arthaḥ, hetv.arthaḥ, uddeśaḥ, nirdeśaḥ, upadeśaḥ, apadeśaḥ, atideśaḥ, pradeśaḥ, upamānam, artha.āpattiḥ, saṃśayaḥ, prasaṅgaḥ, viparyayaḥ, vākya.śeṣaḥ, anumatam, vyākhyānam, nirvacanam, nidarśanam, apavargaḥ, sva.sañjñā, pūrva.pakṣaḥ, uttara.pakṣaḥ, eka.antaḥ, anāgata.avekṣaṇam, atikrānta.avekṣaṇam, niyogaḥ, vikalpaḥ, samuccayaḥ ūhyam iti

hindi: जिस विषय को लेकर कुछ कहा जाता है, वह अधिकरण है।
english: The matter with reference to which [something] is said is the adhikaraṇa.
notes: adhikṛtya = 'having made the topic / taking up'; the object of the saying is not stated.

words.gram: n. nom. pl. pp. caus. pra-√sthā
n. nom. sg. pp. √kṛ (agrees with artha-śāstram)

hindi: “पृथ्वी की प्राप्ति और पालन के लिए पूर्व आचार्यों ने जितने अर्थशास्त्र प्रस्तुत किए हैं, उनका प्रायः संग्रह करके यह एक अर्थशास्त्र रचा गया है।”
english: “Having, for the most part, collected those treatises on artha, as many as have been propounded by earlier teachers for the acquisition and protection of the earth, this one Arthaśāstra has been made.”
notes: Quoted sentence; closing 'iti' is rendered by the quotation marks only. 'tāni' is the correlative of 'yāvanti'. 'prāyaśaḥ' could also be taken with 'prasthāpitāni' (propounded for the most part); the first is preferred.
lines_deva: "पृथिव्या लाभे पालने च यावन्त्य् अर्थ.शास्त्राणि पूर्व.आचार्यैः प्रस्थापितानि प्रायशस् तानि संहृत्य-एकम् इदम् अर्थ.शास्त्रं कृतम्" इति
lines_iast: "pṛthivyā lābhe pālane ca yāvanty artha.śāstrāṇi pūrva.ācāryaiḥ prasthāpitāni prāyaśas tāni saṃhṛtya-ekam idam artha.śāstraṃ kṛtam" iti

hindi: शास्त्र के प्रकरणों का क्रम विधान है।
english: The sequence of the sections of a treatise is the vidhāna.
notes: Hindi/English 'of the sections' follows the compound prakaraṇa-anupūrvī (sequence of prakaraṇas).

hindi: “विद्याओं का उल्लेख, वृद्धों का संयोग, इन्द्रियों पर विजय, अमात्यों की उत्पत्ति” — इस प्रकार से आरम्भ होने वाला।
english: “Enumeration of the sciences, association with the aged, conquest of the senses, origin of ministers” — [the sequence] beginning thus.
notes: Predicate of the unit is 'vidhānam' in unit 6. 'samuddeśa' = enumeration / designation; 'amātya-utpatti' literally 'origin of ministers' (alternative 'creation of ministers'). The e-text spells 'samyogaḥ' (m, not anusvāra).
lines_deva: "विद्या.समुद्देशः, वृद्ध.सम्योगः, इन्द्रिय.जयः, अमात्य.उत्पत्तिः" इत्य् एवं.आदिकम् इति
lines_iast: "vidyā.samuddeśaḥ, vṛddha.samyogaḥ, indriya.jayaḥ, amātya.utpattiḥ" ity evaṃ.ādikam iti

hindi: वाक्यों का जोड़ना योग है।
english: The joining of sentences is the yoga.

hindi: “लोक चार वर्णों और आश्रमों वाला है।”
english: “The world has four varṇas and āśramas.”
notes: catur may go with both varṇa and āśrama (four varṇas and four āśramas), as printed 'catur.varṇa.āśrama'. Example sentence for yoga; closing iti rendered by the quotation marks.

words.gloss: having the word as its limit

hindi: जिसकी सीमा पद है, वह पदार्थ है।
english: The padārtha (meaning of a word) is that which has the word as its limit.
notes: Obscure definition. 'avadhika' = 'having a limit/boundary'; alternative 'limited to the word / extending only up to the word'. Rendered literally.

words.gram: m. (quoted word, stem form as printed; not nominative)

hindi: ‘मूलहर’ — यह पद है।
english: ‘mūla-hara’ is a word.
notes: Example of a pada. The stem form 'hara' is as printed; the next unit gives 'mūla.haraḥ'.

words.gram: m. acc. sg. (dvandva; adjective agreeing with artham)

hindi: “जो पिता और पितामह के धन को अन्याय से खा जाता है, वह मूलहर है” — यह अर्थ है।
english: “He who unjustly consumes the wealth of [his] father and grandfather is a mūla-hara” — such is the meaning.
notes: 'mūla-hara' is left untranslated as a term (literally 'root-taker'). 'pitṛ.paitāmaham' read as an ancestral-wealth compound: father's and grandfather's [wealth]. 'ity arthaḥ' as in unit 1.
lines_deva: "यः पितृ.पैतामहम् अर्थम् अन्यायेन भक्षयति स मूल.हरः" इत्य् अर्थः
lines_iast: "yaḥ pitṛ.paitāmaham artham anyāyena bhakṣayati sa mūla.haraḥ" ity arthaḥ

hindi: जो हेतु अर्थ को सिद्ध करता है, वह हेत्वर्थ है।
english: A reason that accomplishes the matter is the hetv-artha.
notes: 'artha-sādhaka' is literal; alternatives 'establishing the point in question' or 'accomplishing the purpose'.

hindi: “क्योंकि धर्म और काम का मूल अर्थ है।”
english: “For dharma and kāma (desire) have artha as their root.”
notes: Example of a hetvartha. Closing iti rendered by the quotation marks.

hindi: संक्षिप्त वाक्य उद्देश है।
english: A concise statement is the uddeśa.
notes: 'samāsa' = brief / condensed (not the grammatical compound).

hindi: “विद्या और विनय का कारण इन्द्रियों पर विजय है।”
english: “The conquest of the senses is the cause of learning and discipline.”

hindi: विस्तृत वाक्य निर्देश है।
english: A detailed statement is the nirdeśa.
notes: 'vyāsa' here is taken as 'expansion, detail', not the personal name.

hindi: “कान, त्वचा, आँख, जीभ और नाक इन्द्रियों का शब्द, स्पर्श, रूप, रस और गन्ध में विचलित न होना इन्द्रियजय है।”
english: “The conquest of the senses is the not going astray of the organs of ear, skin, eye, tongue and nose in respect of sound, touch, form, taste and smell.”

text_flags.why: possible: no space between the closing quotation mark and iti

notes: 'avipratipatti' (a-vi-prati-pad) is literally 'absence of wrong / contrary engagement'; alternatives 'non-contrariety', 'non-perversity'. Rendered 'not going astray' (Hindi 'विचलित न होना'). The last token contains two words fused without space.

hindi: ‘इस प्रकार आचरण करना चाहिए’ — यह उपदेश है।
english: “[One] should act thus” — this is the upadeśa.
notes: vartitavyam is an impersonal gerundive; the agent is not stated.

hindi: “धर्म और अर्थ का विरोध किए बिना काम का सेवन करे; सुखहीन न हो।”
english: “[One] should pursue desire (kāma) without conflict with dharma and artha; [one] should not be without happiness.”

text_flags.why: probable: the sense requires a-virodhena (without conflict); as printed "virodhena" would mean with conflict, which contradicts the next clause; one a seems dropped (dharma.artha + avirodhena)
possible: written with h instead of the visarga

notes: Translated with the corrected reading avirodhena. If virodhena were kept literally the sense would be 'with conflict with dharma and artha'.
lines_deva: "धर्म.अर्थ.विरोधेन कामं सेवेत, न निह्सुखः स्यात्" इति
lines_iast: "dharma.artha.virodhena kāmaṃ seveta, na nihsukhaḥ syāt" iti

hindi: ‘ऐसा उसने कहा है’ — यह अपदेश है।
english: “Thus that one has said” — this is the apadeśa.
notes: 'asau' = 'that one' (the authority being cited).

hindi: “बारह अमात्यों की मन्त्रिपरिषद् बनाए,” ऐसा मानव कहते हैं; “सोलह,” ऐसा बार्हस्पत्य कहते हैं; “बीस,” ऐसा औशनस कहते हैं; “सामर्थ्य के अनुसार,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “[One] should form a council of counsellors [consisting of] twelve ministers,” say the Manavas; “sixteen,” say the Barhaspatyas; “twenty,” say the Ausanasas; “according to capacity,” says Kautilya.
notes: Mānavāḥ, Bārhaspatyāḥ, Auśanasāḥ are the followers/school of Manu, Brihaspati and Usanas; kept as names in the glossary style. The accusatives mantri-pariṣadam and dvādaśa-amātyān are read together ('a council of counsellors of twelve ministers'); 'kurvīta' could also be 'should make (appoint)'. The final iti closes the whole quotation and is shown by the quotation mark. The dashes are the editors' punctuation.
lines_deva: "मन्त्रि.परिषदं द्वादश.अमात्यान् कुर्वीत-इति मानवाः - षोडश-इति बार्हस्पत्याः - विंशतिम् इत्य् औशनसाः - यथा.सामर्थ्यम् इति कौटिल्यः" इति
lines_iast: "mantri.pariṣadaṃ dvādaśa.amātyān kurvīta-iti mānavāḥ - ṣoḍaśa-iti bārhaspatyāḥ - viṃśatim ity auśanasāḥ - yathā.sāmarthyam iti kauṭilyaḥ" iti

hindi: कहे हुए से सिद्ध करना अतिदेश है।
english: Establishing by what has been stated is the atideśa.
notes: The thing established is not stated in the Sanskrit.

hindi: “दिए हुए का न देना ऋण-आदान से समझाया जा चुका है।”
english: “The non-giving of what was given has been explained by ṛṇa-ādāna (the taking of debt).”
notes: ṛṇa-ādāna is probably the name of a topic (cross-reference to the section on debts); literal sense 'taking of debt' (alternative 'recovery of debt'). 'dattasya apradānam' is literal; the sense (non-repayment/non-delivery) is not fixed by the text.

words.gloss: by what is to be stated

hindi: जो कहा जाना है, उससे सिद्ध करना प्रदेश है।
english: Establishing by what is to be stated is the pradeśa.

hindi: “अथवा साम, दान, भेद और दण्ड से, जैसा हम आपत्तियों में बताएँगे।”
english: “Or by conciliation, gifts, dissension [and] force, as we shall explain in adversities.”
notes: 'āpatsu' may also be a topic heading (the section on adversities); rendered literally.

hindi: देखे हुए से अनदेखे को सिद्ध करना उपमान है।
english: Establishing the unseen by the seen is the upamāna.

hindi: “जिनकी छूट समाप्त हो गई है, उन पर पिता के समान अनुग्रह करे।”
english: “[One] should favour, like a father, those whose exemptions have ended.”
notes: 'parihāra' is rendered 'exemption' (alternative 'avoidance, remission'); the kind of exemption is not stated here.

hindi: जो कही नहीं गई बात अर्थ से प्राप्त होती है, वह अर्थापत्ति है।
english: That which is unstated and comes about from the sense is the arthāpatti.

words.gloss: by way of the agreeable and beneficial

hindi: “लोक-व्यवहार को जानने वाला, स्वयं, द्रव्य और प्रकृति से सम्पन्न राजा का आश्रय प्रिय और हित के द्वारा ले।”
english: “One who knows the ways of the world should resort to a king endowed with self, resources and constituent elements, by way of the agreeable and beneficial.”
notes: ātma-dravya-prakṛti-sampanna is read as a dvandva (self, resources, constituent elements); another reading takes dravya-prakṛti as the technical 'material constituents'. No closing 'iti' in this unit; the quotation ends with the mark.

words.gloss: by way of the disagreeable and beneficial
words.gram: n. inst. sg. (apriya-hita + dvāra; apriya-hita read as dvandva, or as 'disagreeable yet beneficial': uncertain)

hindi: “अप्रिय और हित के द्वारा आश्रय न ले” — यह बात अर्थ से प्राप्त होती है।
english: “[One] should not resort by way of the disagreeable and beneficial” — [this] is obtained from the sense.
notes: 'apriya-hita' is read as a dvandva (disagreeable-and-beneficial), the implied negation of the priya-hita of unit 30; the alternative a-priya-a-hita is not supported by the printed form. Compound analysis of apriya-hita is uncertain (dvandva 'disagreeable and beneficial' as drafted, or 'disagreeable yet beneficial'); English keeps the literal members. The final iti after bhavati closes the sentence and is not rendered.

hindi: दोनों ओर हेतु वाला विषय संशय है।
english: A matter having a reason on both sides is the saṃśaya (doubt).

hindi: “जिसकी प्रकृतियाँ क्षीण और लोभी हैं अथवा जिसकी प्रकृतियों के साथ अनुचित व्यवहार हुआ है।”
english: “[A king] whose constituent elements are impoverished and greedy, or whose constituent elements have been wronged.”
notes: Elliptical example of a saṃśaya (no verb or noun king stated; the supplied 'king' is from unit 30). 'apacarita' = 'wronged, ill-treated' (alternative 'gone astray'). Closing iti rendered by the quotation marks.

hindi: दूसरे प्रकरण के साथ समान विषय प्रसङ्ग है।
english: A matter that is common with another section is the prasaṅga.
notes: samāna with the instrumental: 'same as / common with'.

words.gloss: assigned for the work of farming

hindi: “‘कृषि-कर्म के लिए निर्दिष्ट भूमि पर’ — यह पहले के समान है।”
english: “‘On the land assigned for the work of farming’ — this is the same as the former.”
notes: Example of a prasaṅga: the cited phrase 'kṛṣi-karma-pradiṣṭāyāṃ bhūmau' is declared the same as an earlier statement. 'kṛṣi-karma' = farming work, literal. The first iti closes the cited phrase.

hindi: उलटे से सिद्ध करना विपर्यय है।
english: Establishing by the reverse is the viparyaya.

hindi: “असन्तुष्ट के लिए उलटा।”
english: “The opposite [holds] for the dissatisfied.”
notes: Elliptical; no verb is stated. viparīta = opposite, reversed. What is reversed is not stated in this unit, so '[holds]' is only a bracketed placeholder.

hindi: जिससे वाक्य पूरा किया जाता है, वह वाक्यशेष है।
english: That by which a sentence is completed is the remainder of the sentence (vākya-śeṣa).

words.gloss: of one whose wings are cut

hindi: “कटे पंखों वाले के समान, और राजा की चेष्टा का नाश।”
english: “Like one whose wings are cut, and the king's loss of movement.”
notes: The quotation is incomplete; the next unit says the missing word is śakuneḥ ('of a bird'). Hindi/English supply nothing beyond the quoted words.

hindi: वहाँ “पक्षी का” यह वाक्यशेष है।
english: There “of a bird” is the remainder of the sentence.

hindi: दूसरे का वाक्य, जिसका निषेध नहीं किया गया, अनुमत है।
english: Another's statement that is not rejected is approved (anumata).
notes: para may also be 'the opponent's'; rendered literally as 'another's'.

hindi: “दो पक्ष, उरस्य, प्रतिग्रह — यह औशनस मत का व्यूह-विभाग है।”
english: “Two wings, the centre, the reserve: thus [is] the division of the array of the school of Usanas.”
lines_deva: "पक्षाव् उरस्यं प्रतिग्रह इत्य् औशनसो व्यूह.विभागः" इति
lines_iast: "pakṣāv urasyaṃ pratigraha ity auśanaso vyūha.vibhāgaḥ" iti

hindi: अतिशय का वर्णन व्याख्यान है।
english: Description of excess (atiśaya) is explanation (vyākhyāna).
notes: atiśaya is rendered literally as 'excess'; the sense may be 'detailed/further description' or 'description of the special point'.

words.gloss: of those following the dharma of a saṅgha

hindi: “और विशेष रूप से संघों का, संघ-धर्म वालों का और राजकुलों का जुए के कारण भेद और उसके कारण विनाश — इस प्रकार शासन की दुर्बलता के कारण असत् का प्रग्रह व्यसनों में सबसे बुरा है।”
english: “And especially of saṅghas, of those following the dharma of a saṅgha, and of royal houses, [there is] dissension caused by gambling, [and] destruction caused by that; thus favouring of the bad is the worst of the vices (vyasana), owing to weakness of the administration.”
notes: vyasana here = vice (the king's own), not calamity of a constituent element. saṅgha-dharmin is rendered literally; it may mean 'having the constitution of a saṅgha'. asat-pragraha follows the glossary ('favouring of the bad'); 'association with the bad' is possible. The genitives are rendered literally ('of saṅghas ...').
lines_deva: "विशेषतश् च सङ्घानां सङ्घ.धर्मिणां च राज.कुलानां द्यूत.निमित्तो भेदस् तन्.निमित्तो विनाश इत्य् असत्.प्रग्रहः पापिष्ठतमो व्यसनानां तन्त्र.दौर्बल्यात्" इति
lines_iast: "viśeṣataś ca saṅghānāṃ saṅgha.dharmiṇāṃ ca rāja.kulānāṃ dyūta.nimitto bhedas tan.nimitto vināśa ity asat.pragrahaḥ pāpiṣṭhatamo vyasanānāṃ tantra.daurbalyāt" iti

hindi: गुण से शब्द की निष्पत्ति निर्वचन है।
english: Derivation of a word from quality is etymology (nirvacana).

hindi: “यह इसे श्रेय से दूर फेंकता है — इस प्रकार व्यसन।”
english: “It throws him away from the better; thus [it is] vyasana.”
notes: An etymology of vyasana (vi-√as). Rendered 'from the better' for śreyas; 'from the good/welfare' is the alternative.

hindi: दृष्टान्त, दृष्टान्त से युक्त, निदर्शन है।
english: An example, one joined with an example, is illustration (nidarśana).
notes: The relation of the three words is not certain (the second may mean 'accompanied by its application'). Rendered literally.

hindi: “क्योंकि बड़े से विग्रह में पड़ा हुआ मानो हाथी के साथ पैदल युद्ध को अपनाता है।”
english: “For one who is at war with a greater one takes on, as it were, a fight on foot with an elephant.”
notes: jyāyas = greater (stronger, older); 'greater' kept. The e-text writes 'iva.abhyupaiti' with a dot though iva + abhyupaiti is two words. hastinā is taken with pāda-yuddham ('fight on foot with an elephant').
lines_deva: "विगृहीतो हि ज्यायसा हस्तिना पाद.युद्धम् इव.अभ्युपैति" इति
lines_iast: "vigṛhīto hi jyāyasā hastinā pāda.yuddham iva.abhyupaiti" iti

hindi: आक्रान्त को अलग खींच लेना अपवर्ग है।
english: Drawing away of the overrun is apavarga.
notes: abhipluta = overrun, overwhelmed (p.p.p. abhi-√plu); vyapakarṣaṇa = drawing away. The technical sense is not certain; apavarga is left untranslated.

hindi: “पास की शत्रु-सेना को सदा बसाए, सिवाय भीतरी कोप की आशंका के।”
english: “One should always settle the near army of the enemy, except for suspicion of internal revolt.”
notes: vāsayet = causes to dwell; the object and purpose are not stated. anyatra + ablative = 'except (for)'. kopa = revolt as in glossary 8.2.

hindi: दूसरों द्वारा स्वीकार न किया गया शब्द अपनी संज्ञा है।
english: A word not agreed by others is an own designation (sva-sañjñā).
notes: asamita is obscure: 'not agreed upon / not shared / not used by others'. A misprint for asaṃmita ('not approved') is possible. Rendered literally.

hindi: “पहली प्रकृति; उसकी, भूमि में अनन्तर वाली दूसरी, एक भूमि के अन्तर वाली तीसरी।”
english: “The first constituent element; of him the one next in land [is] the second, the one with one land between [is] the third.”
notes: prakṛti here refers to the members of the ring of kings, not to the seven constituents of 6.1; glossary 'constituent element' kept. Whether prakṛti means 'constituent' or 'member of the circle' is for the reviewer. Reviewer: prathamā agrees with prakṛtiḥ ('the first constituent element'); the glossary term is kept for the members of the circle.
lines_deva: "प्रथमा प्रकृतिः, तस्य भूम्य्.अनन्तरा द्वितीया, भूम्य्.एक.अन्तरा तृतीया" इति
lines_iast: "prathamā prakṛtiḥ, tasya bhūmy.anantarā dvitīyā, bhūmy.eka.antarā tṛtīyā" iti

hindi: जिस वाक्य का निषेध किया जाना है, वह पूर्वपक्ष है।
english: A statement to be rejected is the pūrva-pakṣa (the first side).

words.gloss: of the calamities of the king and the minister
words.gram: dvandva in tat-puruṣa, n. gen. du.

hindi: “राजा और अमात्य के व्यसनों में अमात्य का व्यसन अधिक गम्भीर है।”
english: “Of the calamities of the king and the minister, the calamity of the minister is more serious.”

hindi: उसका निर्णय करने वाला वाक्य उत्तरपक्ष है।
english: The statement deciding that is the uttara-pakṣa (the later side).
notes: uttara may also be 'reply'; rendered literally as 'later'.

words.gloss: standing in the place of the peak of that

hindi: “उस पर निर्भर होने के कारण; क्योंकि राजा उसके शिखर के स्थान पर है।”
english: “Because of dependence on that; for the king stands in the place of the peak of that.”
notes: 'that' (tad) is not named in the unit; it refers back to the minister of the preceding quotation. kūṭa = peak/top; 'heap' or 'chief part' are alternatives.

hindi: जो सर्वत्र आश्रित है, वह एकान्त है।
english: [That which is] dependent everywhere is ekānta (lit. 'one-ended').
notes: The sense of āyatta ('dependent / holding good') and of ekānta ('exclusive, absolute') in this definition is uncertain; rendered literally. Hindi supplies the relative 'jo/vah' for the missing subject.

hindi: “इसलिए अपना उद्योग करे।”
english: “Therefore one should make one's own exertion.”
notes: utthāna = rising, exertion; 'exertion' chosen. The subject of kurvīta is not stated.

words.gloss: looking to what has not yet come

hindi: “बाद में ऐसा विहित है” — यह अनागत का अवलोकन है।
english: “Afterwards it is thus laid down”: [this is] looking to what has not yet come (anāgata-avekṣaṇa).

hindi: “तुला और प्रतिमान को पौतव-अध्यक्ष के विषय में कहेंगे।”
english: “We shall state balance and weights in [the section on] the pautava superintendent.”
notes: pautava is left untranslated (traditionally a department of weights and measures, but the line does not say so). The locative is rendered with a bracketed supply in English.

words.gloss: looking to what has gone by

hindi: “पहले ऐसा विहित है” — यह अतीत का अवलोकन है।
english: “Before, it is thus laid down”: [this is] looking to what has gone by (atikrānta-avekṣaṇa).

text_flags.why: possible typo: ṣk for kṣ; compare anāgata.avekṣaṇam in unit 59 and the sense 'looking'

notes: The printed spelling 'aveṣkaṇam' is read as avekṣaṇam.

hindi: “अमात्य की सम्पत् पहले कही जा चुकी है।”
english: “The excellence of the minister has been stated before.”

hindi: “ऐसे, अन्यथा नहीं” — यह नियोग है।
english: “Thus, not otherwise”: this [is] niyoga (command).
notes: niyoga = binding command / appointment; kept as a term.

hindi: “इसलिए इसे धर्म्य और अर्थ्य का उपदेश दे, अधर्म्य और अनर्थ्य का नहीं।”
english: “Therefore one should advise him [what is] in accordance with dharma and profitable, and not [what is] contrary to dharma and unprofitable.”

text_flags.why: typo: letters ay transposed; parallel to arthyam earlier in the line

notes: asya is taken as 'to him' (dative sense of the genitive); the subject of upadiśet is not stated.
lines_deva: "तस्माद् धर्म्यम् अर्थ्यं च-अस्य-उपदिशेत्, न-अधर्म्यम् अनर्थय्म् च" इति
lines_iast: "tasmād dharmyam arthyaṃ ca-asya-upadiśet, na-adharmyam anarthaym ca" iti

hindi: “इससे या इससे” — यह विकल्प है।
english: “By this or by this”: [this is] option (vikalpa).

hindi: “अथवा सबसे धर्मिष्ठ विवाहों में उत्पन्न पुत्रियाँ।”
english: “Or daughters born in the most righteous marriages.”
notes: A fragment of a longer quotation.

hindi: “इससे और इससे” — यह समुच्चय है।
english: “By this and by this”: [this is] combination (samuccaya).

hindi: “स्वयंजात पिता का और बन्धुओं का दायाद है।”
english: “The self-born is heir of the father and of the kinsmen.”
notes: svayañjāta is rendered literally; its technical sense is not given in the line and is not guessed here.

hindi: न कहे हुए का करना ऊह्य है।
english: The doing of what is unsaid is ūhya (to be inferred).
notes: ūhya may be the name of the device or the gerundive 'to be inferred'; both are kept.

hindi: “जिस प्रकार दाता और प्रतिग्रहीता की हानि न हो, उसी प्रकार कुशल लोग अनुशय की व्यवस्था करें।”
english: “In such a way that the giver and the receiver may not be harmed, so should the skilled arrange the anuśaya.”
notes: anuśaya is kept untranslated: it may mean 'regret/remorse' or the revocation of a transaction. kalpayeyuḥ rendered 'arrange'.
lines_deva: "यथा च दाता प्रतिग्रहीता च न-उपहतौ स्यातां तथा-अनुशयं कुशलाः कल्पयेयुः" इति
lines_iast: "yathā ca dātā pratigrahītā ca na-upahatau syātāṃ tathā-anuśayaṃ kuśalāḥ kalpayeyuḥ" iti

words.gloss: with the tantra-yuktis (methods of the treatise)

hindi: इस प्रकार यह शास्त्र इन तन्त्रयुक्तियों से युक्त है; इस लोक और परलोक की प्राप्ति और रक्षा के लिए कहा गया है।
english: Thus this treatise, furnished with these tantra-yuktis (methods of the treatise), has been stated for the acquisition and the protection of this world and the other.
notes: tantra here is 'treatise/system', not 'administration' as in the glossary for 8.3. 'for' renders the locatives avāptau pālane. parasya is taken as 'of the other [world]'.
lines_deva: एवं शास्त्रम् इदं युक्तम् एताभिस् तन्त्र.युक्तिभिः
अवाप्तौ पालने च-उक्तं लोकस्य-अस्य परस्य च
lines_iast: evaṃ śāstram idaṃ yuktam etābhis tantra.yuktibhiḥ
avāptau pālane ca-uktaṃ lokasya-asya parasya ca

hindi: यह शास्त्र धर्म, अर्थ और काम को प्रवृत्त करता है और रक्षा करता है; और अधर्म, अनर्थ और विद्वेष का नाश करता है।
english: This treatise sets in motion dharma, wealth and desire, and protects [them]; and it destroys unrighteousness, loss and hatred.
notes: pravartayati may be 'promotes'. anartha is rendered 'loss' (opposite of artha; compare anarthyam 'unprofitable' in unit 64). The object of pāti is not stated.
lines_deva: धर्मम् अर्थं च कामं च प्रवर्तयति पाति च
lines_iast: dharmam arthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca pravartayati pāti ca

hindi: जिसने अमर्ष से शास्त्र, शस्त्र और नन्द राजा के पास गई पृथ्वी का शीघ्र उद्धार किया, उसने यह शास्त्र बनाया।
english: By whom the śāstra, the weapon and the earth that had gone to the Nanda king were quickly rescued through indignation, by him this treatise was made.
notes: The person is not named in the unit. The first śāstra (learning) is kept as 'śāstra' to keep it apart from 'this treatise'.
lines_deva: येन शास्त्रं च शस्त्रं च नन्द.राज.गता च भूः
अमर्षेण-उद्धृतान्य् आशु तेन शास्त्रम् इदं कृतम्
lines_iast: yena śāstraṃ ca śastraṃ ca nanda.rāja.gatā ca bhūḥ
amarṣeṇa-uddhṛtāny āśu tena śāstram idaṃ kṛtam
